extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of bulk gasoline terminals, environmental compliance staff, control device manufacturers, state regulators, and permit writers
extracted.subtask_short: NSPS subpart XXa gasoline loading racks
extracted.subtask_description: Federal NSPS (New Source Performance Standards) requirements and compliance provisions for gasoline loading racks and associated equipment at bulk gasoline terminals, including numeric TOC/ppm limits, monitoring/averaging rules, affected-facility definitions, and monitoring/recordkeeping provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric TOC emission limits for loading racks
rubrics_metrics.description: Final emission limits in NSPS subpart XXa are 1.0 mg/L non-methane TOC for new sources and 10 mg/L non-methane TOC for modified and reconstructed sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities may choose to comply using direct TOC measurements without correcting for methane content only if measuring/adjusting according to EPA-approved methods. The 1.0 mg/L and 10 mg/L values reflect the BSER determinations and cost-effectiveness analyses described in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration-equivalent limits for VRU-controlled systems
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems controlled with vapor recovery units (VRUs), the equivalent concentration limits are 550 ppmv TOC (as propane) for new facilities and 5,500 ppmv TOC (as propane) for modified/reconstructed facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concentration limits are expressed on a 3-hour rolling average because they are directly enforceable with common VRU monitoring systems. The EPA determined these to be equivalent to the 1.0 and 10 mg/L TOC limits respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance to exclude methane from measured TOC
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule allows exclusion of methane contribution from measured TOC (i.e., non-methane TOC limits) if measured according to EPA-approved methods; ethane exclusion is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping and reporting requirements correspond to the methane exclusion. The rule explains instrumentation limitations (e.g., NDIR can correct for methane but not ethane) and rationale (methane is not well-controlled by carbon adsorption), and notes that source test summaries may not report methane concentrations so facilities must follow approved methods and report whether their method corrects for methane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affected facility definitions (two separate affected facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two affected facility definitions are finalized: (1) 'gasoline loading rack affected facility' — the total of all loading racks at a bulk gasoline terminal that deliver liquid into gasoline cargo tanks, including gasoline loading racks, vapor collection systems, and vapor processing system; (2) 'collection of equipment at a bulk gasoline terminal affected facility' — all equipment associated with loading of gasoline including lines and pumps transferring gasoline from storage vessels, loading racks, vapor collection systems, and vapor processing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loading rack emission limits apply to the gasoline loading rack affected facility; adding equipment in the tank farm area will not trigger loading rack requirements but will trigger applicability for the equipment leak monitoring provisions under the collection-of-equipment definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3-hour rolling average definition and valid data rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The 3-hour rolling average is retained for CEMS and operating parameters, but the rule clarifies what constitutes valid data depending on the control device: for VRUs the 3-hour rolling average applies during all periods when the VRU is operating (may include times with no active liquid loading); for thermal oxidation systems the 3-hour rolling average applies when liquid product is loaded into gasoline cargo tanks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thermal oxidizers: exclude periods when no liquid product is being loaded. VRUs: include periods when the VRU is online and capable of processing vapors. The 3-hour choice aligns with the duration of the CEMS performance evaluation (minimum ~189 minutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: CEMS performance evaluation and averaging basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of VRUs must conduct performance evaluations of their TOC CEMS consisting of at least nine test runs, each a sampling traverse of minimum 21 minutes (minimum 189 minutes total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 3-hour rolling average was selected to be consistent with this performance evaluation duration. For thermal oxidation system performance testing, the performance test is 6 hours; however, there is no longer a performance test for VRUs, hence the CEMS evaluation is the relevant basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring/valid data inclusion when previous cargo tank contents are known
rubrics_metrics.description: If owner/operator has information on previous cargo tank contents, they may exclude from the 3-hour rolling average periods when there is liquid product being loaded but there are no gasoline cargo tanks being loaded. If no information is available, assume loading is into a gasoline cargo tank and include those periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition changes throughout rules to use the phrase 'loading liquid product into a gasoline cargo tank' to account for previous-load considerations and ensure conservative applicability when prior contents are unknown.

rubrics_metrics.name: VRU operation to minimize air or nitrogen intrusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must 'operate the vapor recovery system to minimize air or nitrogen intrusion except as needed for the system to operate as designed for the purpose of removing VOC from the adsorption media or to break vacuum in the system and bring the system back to atmospheric pressure.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the stricter proposed requirement that only vacuum breaker valves be used. The rule also reiterates that use of gaseous diluents to achieve compliance with concentration-based standards is prohibited (consistent with §60.12). The change acknowledges necessary purge air during regeneration cycles of VRUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare monitoring alternative for thermal oxidation systems (10 mg/L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flare monitoring provisions consistent with Refinery NESHAP (40 CFR 63.670) are acceptable as a compliance alternative for thermal oxidation systems used to meet the 10 mg/L TOC limit for modified and reconstructed sources (but not for new sources subject to the 1 mg/L limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA concluded enclosed combustors/thermal oxidizers are commensurate with 10 mg/L and that flare monitoring provisions are reasonable. This permits use of the existing flare monitoring approach with the caveats and operating limits discussed (e.g., NHV limits, loading-ratio demonstration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Net heating value (NHV) operating limits and exemption application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an exemption from monitoring under 40 CFR 63.670(j)(6) must include a minimum ratio of gasoline loaded to total liquid product loaded and, if perimeter air-assisted, a minimum gasoline loading rate; testing must collect samples at conditions expected to produce the flare gas with the lowest net heating value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If testing shows vent gas NHV meets or exceeds NHV_cz or NHV_dil limits, compliance with the minimum gasoline loading ratio or minimum gasoline loading rate can be used to demonstrate compliance. Facilities must operate at or above the minimums in the application whenever liquid product is loaded into cargo tanks for which vapors are routed to the flare/thermal oxidation system. The rule clarifies how these provisions apply when multiple product types are loaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time net heating value determination and use of single/95th percentile value
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with 40 CFR 63.670(j)(6)(i)(F), a single value for the vent gas net heating value (either the lowest single value or the 95th percentile confidence value) must be used for all vent gas flow rates, based on sampling conducted consistent with the application under 63.670(j)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule combines proposed sampling protocols and requires a single assessment (now consolidated in 40 CFR 60.502a(c)(3)(viii)) that determines quantity of supplemental fuel needed to demonstrate continuous compliance. Fewer facilities are expected to need the minimum supplemental gas addition rate option because of the minimum ratio/loading rate provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation method for loading rate operating limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Loading rate operating limits (and analogous loading-ratio limits) are to be monitored on 5-minute block periods and calculated on a rolling 15-minute period across three contiguous 5-minute block periods, considering only periods when liquid product is loaded into gasoline cargo tanks for any portion of those blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'contiguous' is used to emphasize there must be no break between the 5-minute blocks (unlike 'consecutive' in the 3-hour rolling average definition). If any 5-minute block has no liquid product loaded into gasoline cargo tanks, the previous rolling 15-minute period ends and the next rolling period begins only when three contiguous 5-minute blocks with loading occur. This addresses end-of-loading edge cases and aligns operating-limit evaluation with intermittent loading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of flare tip velocity assessment records
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators may comply with the flare tip velocity limit using a one-time design evaluation (engineering assessment) demonstrating the flare tip velocity would always be below 60 feet per second based on maximum loading rate and flare tip diameter; records of this assessment must be maintained for as long as this compliance provision is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA agrees that with low-pressure gasoline loading the flare tip velocity limit is unlikely to be exceeded; where demonstrated by design evaluation, continuous net heating value measurements and flow monitoring may not be needed for demonstrating compliance with the flare tip velocity limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using gaseous diluents for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with §60.12, the use of gaseous diluents to achieve compliance with a standard that is based on concentration of a pollutant in gases discharged to the atmosphere is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated alongside the VRU air/nitrogen intrusion language to prevent facilities from introducing diluents (air or nitrogen) to reduce measured concentrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of equipment leak provisions via collection-of-equipment affected facility
rubrics_metrics.description: By defining a 'collection of equipment at a bulk gasoline terminal affected facility', the final rule ensures all equipment associated with loading gasoline (lines, pumps, storage-transfer equipment) is subject to equipment leak monitoring requirements under NSPS subpart XXa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means new equipment in tank farms will trigger NSPS subpart XXa applicability for equipment leak requirements even if that new equipment does not trigger loading rack control requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirement: operate at or above application minimums when loading
rubrics_metrics.description: If a facility relies on minimum gasoline loading ratios or minimum gasoline loading rates established in its application to demonstrate compliance with NHV operating limits, the affected source must operate at or above those minimum values at all times when liquid product is loaded into cargo tanks whose vapors are sent to the flare/thermal oxidation system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes the minimums de facto operating limits; compliance demonstrations and continuous compliance rely on maintaining these minimums during loading events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping/reporting for methane-correction status of measurement methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule requires recordkeeping and reporting that indicate whether the measurement method used in performance tests or CEMS corrects for methane concentration when facilities elect to exclude methane from TOC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities must document and report whether their performance tests or continuous monitoring correct for methane, since exclusion affects the applicable numeric limits (non-methane TOC basis).
